statement: For every odd prime p>3, let r be computed from A,B in F_p by equation (4) of arXiv:2609.05371v1 using their canonical representatives, and let Nhat_p(A,B) be given by equation (5). Then the universal assertion that Nhat_p(A,B) equals the number of affine pairs (x,y) in F_p^2 satisfying y^2=x^3+Ax+B for every A,B in F_p holds if and only if p>=17. The sufficient direction is Theorem 3 of the cited paper. Necessity is witnessed, for p=5,7,11,13 respectively, by (A,B)=(1,1),(0,1),(1,3),(0,4), for which (N,r,Nhat)=(8,2,3),(11,3,4),(17,5,6),(20,6,7).
contribution: This resolves the full supervisor-generated sharp-threshold question by coupling the published universal theorem for p>=17 with transparent exact coefficient extractions and complete affine residue tables for one nonsingular counterexample at each of the four smaller admissible primes. The upper-range theorem is prior work; no claim of priority is made for the short sharpness corollary beyond the documented bounded literature search.
